rules.explanation: Wind, a curious cat or a predator can open an unlatched door.
rules.remediation: Choose a latch: a hasp or keyed latch for human doors, a slide bolt for hatches.
rules.title: Door or hatch has no latch

rules.explanation: A door left ajar for a moment is the most common way cats escape from catios.
rules.remediation: Use self-closing spring hinges on human doors.
rules.title: Door does not close by itself

rules.explanation: A gravity latch on a door cats can push from inside may be nudged open.
rules.remediation: Use a hasp, slide bolt or keyed latch, or a second latch at cat height.
rules.title: Gravity latch on an outward-opening door

rules.explanation: Walk-in catios need a door you can pass through with a bucket and tools (about 24″ × 60″ or larger).
rules.remediation: Widen or heighten the door.
rules.title: Door is small for cleaning access

rules.explanation: Litter, water, plants and shelves all need regular cleaning; without a door or hatch you cannot reach them.
rules.remediation: Add a human door or a cleaning hatch.
rules.title: No way in to clean

rules.explanation: An attached catio is most used when cats can come and go from the house.
rules.remediation: Add a window-access insert or a cat door through the wall, or connect a tunnel.
rules.title: No cat entrance from the house

rules.explanation: Wide bays or tall 2×2 walls flex, letting mesh sag and fasteners pull out.
rules.remediation: Keep posts within 1.2 m (4 ft) and use 2×3 or 2×4 for walls over 1.5 m.
rules.title: Long spans for this frame

rules.explanation: Corrugated panels need slope to shed water; a flat solid roof ponds and leaks.
rules.remediation: Give the roof at least 1:12 slope (1″ fall per foot) by lowering the front.
rules.title: Solid roof is nearly flat

rules.explanation: A frame member is longer than the longest lumber in the stock lengths, so it would need a splice.
rules.remediation: Shorten the structure, add a post to split the span, or allow longer stock lengths.
rules.title: Member longer than available stock

rules.explanation: This structure type is shown for planning only; its attachment and framing need a site visit.
rules.remediation: Use it to explore ideas and share them; ask a builder for a site-specific plan.
rules.title: Concept-only design

rules.explanation: One or more dimensions are outside the range this template is designed for.
rules.remediation: Bring the dimension back within the shown limits, or split the design into two structures.
rules.title: Outside supported sizes

rules.explanation: A door, hatch or cat opening runs past the end of its wall, above the wall height, or into another opening.
rules.remediation: Move or resize the opening.
rules.title: Opening does not fit

rules.explanation: A shelf, ramp or other item extends past its wall or above the structure.
rules.remediation: Move it, shorten it or lower it.
rules.title: Furnishing does not fit

rules.explanation: Build outputs need measured, confirmed dimensions; typed guesses make wrong cut lists.
rules.remediation: Measure the site, then confirm each key dimension in the Site workspace.
rules.title: Dimensions not confirmed

rules.explanation: The footprint overlaps something marked on the site (a tree, AC unit, hose bib or no-build zone).
rules.remediation: Move or resize the structure, or remove the obstacle from the site if it is gone.
rules.title: Overlaps an obstacle

rules.explanation: A box mounted off the ground puts its whole weight on brackets and wall fasteners.
rules.remediation: Fasten the ledger into studs or masonry (not siding only) and check the brackets’ rated load.
rules.title: Raised structure

rules.explanation: Elevated installations involve fall hazards and structural attachment beyond these checks.
rules.remediation: Have the attachment and supports reviewed by a qualified professional, then record the review.
rules.title: Raised above about 1.8 m — professional review

rules.explanation: Structures over 20 m² or taller than 2.7 m may need a permit and engineered framing.
rules.remediation: Check with your building department and have the framing reviewed, then record the review.
rules.title: Large structure — professional review

rules.explanation: Cats can squeeze through surprisingly small gaps; openings 2″ (50 mm) or wider on the short side let many cats out.
rules.remediation: Choose a mesh with openings of 1″ × 2″ or smaller (1″ × 1″ is the common catio choice).
rules.title: Mesh openings are large enough to escape through

rules.explanation: A kitten or small cat in the household can push through openings wider than about 1″.
rules.remediation: Use ½″ × 1″ mesh, or add a band of smaller mesh along the lower walls.
rules.title: Mesh is wider than kittens and small cats need

rules.explanation: 19-gauge and lighter wire holds cats in but is easier for raccoons and dogs to tear from outside.
rules.remediation: Use 16-gauge or heavier welded wire where predators visit.
rules.title: Light-gauge mesh

rules.explanation: A window or door that is only partly inside the catio opens a gap straight to the outside.
rules.remediation: Move or resize the catio so the opening is fully inside or fully outside it.
rules.title: A house opening straddles the catio edge

rules.explanation: Neither end of the tunnel reaches a house opening or another structure, so cats cannot get in.
rules.remediation: Extend the tunnel to a window, cat door or catio, or add a cat door at one end.
rules.title: Tunnel has no entrance

rules.explanation: A cat that rushes doors can slip past you while you step in to clean.
rules.remediation: Add a vestibule (a small airlock with a second door) in front of the human door.
rules.title: No vestibule for an escape-prone cat

rules.explanation: Cats and predators can dig under a frame that sits on grass or soil.
rules.remediation: Add a mesh ground skirt (an apron laid flat outward and pinned) or set the frame on pavers.
rules.title: No dig barrier on soil

rules.explanation: Pavers alone may not hold a light frame in wind, and gaps open as it shifts.
rules.remediation: Add ground anchors at each corner post.
rules.title: Freestanding frame is not anchored

rules.explanation: Dryer exhaust is hot, full of lint and (for gas dryers) combustion gases; it must vent freely outdoors.
rules.remediation: Move the catio or reroute the dryer vent outside the enclosure (have a professional do any vent work).
rules.title: Dryer vent inside the catio

rules.explanation: Utility workers need unobstructed access to gas and electric meters.
rules.remediation: Keep meters outside the enclosure.
rules.title: Utility meter inside the catio

rules.explanation: A bedroom egress window must stay usable for escape and rescue; enclosing it can block that route.
rules.remediation: Keep egress windows outside the catio, or have the design reviewed by your building department or a fire-safety professional.
rules.title: Emergency escape window inside the catio

rules.explanation: Bathroom, kitchen or appliance vents blow moist or fouled air into the enclosure.
rules.remediation: Check what the vent serves; keep exhaust vents outside the catio.
rules.title: Exhaust vent inside the catio

rules.explanation: Roof runoff will soak the catio floor.
rules.remediation: Redirect the downspout outside the enclosure.
rules.title: Downspout inside the catio

rules.explanation: The catio rises above the wall it attaches to, so the top ledger has nothing to fasten to.
rules.remediation: Lower the catio or attach it to a taller part of the house.
rules.title: Taller than the house wall

rules.explanation: Galvanizing before welding leaves bare weld points that rust sooner.
rules.remediation: Prefer galvanized-after-welding, PVC-coated or stainless mesh for long life.
rules.title: Mesh galvanized before welding

rules.explanation: Untreated wood in ground contact decays quickly, loosening the bottom plate and opening gaps.
rules.remediation: Set the frame on pavers, or use lumber rated for ground contact (AWPA UC4A) for the bottom plates.
rules.title: Untreated lumber touching the ground

rules.explanation: Modern pressure-treated lumber (ACQ / copper azole) is widely used outdoors, but cats should not chew it.
rules.remediation: Seal treated members inside the catio, or use cedar for parts cats can reach.
rules.title: Treated lumber within chewing reach

rules.explanation: Every cut edge of welded wire leaves sharp wire ends.
rules.remediation: File cut ends, fold them over or cover them with trim; wear gloves.
rules.title: Cut mesh ends are sharp

rules.explanation: Jumps of more than about 30 cm between levels are hard on stiff joints.
rules.remediation: Add a ramp or intermediate shelves so each step is 30 cm or less.
rules.title: Big step-ups for a senior or less-mobile cat

rules.explanation: This plant is listed as toxic to cats, with organ damage or death reported (true lilies, sago palm, cardiac-glycoside plants…).
rules.remediation: Remove it from the catio and the home. If a cat may have eaten any part, call your veterinarian or ASPCA Animal Poison Control.
rules.title: Plant can seriously harm cats

rules.explanation: This plant is listed as toxic to cats, usually causing stomach upset or mouth irritation.
rules.remediation: Swap it for a plant with no known issue, or keep it out of the catio.
rules.title: Plant is listed as toxic to cats

rules.explanation: This plant was not found in the reviewed toxicity source, or sources disagree. Missing from a list is not proof of safety.
rules.remediation: Keep it out of chewing reach, or ask your veterinarian before planting it in the catio.
rules.title: Plant safety is unknown

rules.explanation: Toxicity lists cover common plants only, and individual cats can react to plants listed as non-toxic.
rules.remediation: Watch for chewing and call your veterinarian about any symptoms.
rules.title: Plant lists are not exhaustive

rules.explanation: Cats need a secure place to retreat and rest (AAFP/ISFM pillar 1).
rules.remediation: Add a bed, hammock or hideaway cube.
rules.title: No resting or hiding place

rules.explanation: Vertical space lets cats survey their territory and avoid each other.
rules.remediation: Add shelves or a bridge at a second height.
rules.title: Fewer than two perch levels

rules.explanation: With several cats, a single high spot becomes contested; a dead-end perch can trap a cat.
rules.remediation: Add a second perch and a second route (a bridge or ramp) so cats can pass each other.
rules.title: One perch for several cats

rules.explanation: Scratching is a normal behaviour that marks territory and keeps claws healthy.
rules.remediation: Add a sisal scratching post.
rules.title: Nothing to scratch

rules.explanation: Cats in a catio for more than a short visit need water, especially in warm weather.
rules.remediation: Add a shaded water bowl.
rules.title: No water

rules.explanation: Cats prefer food and water away from their toilet area (AAFP/ISFM pillar 2).
rules.remediation: Keep at least 1 m between the litter enclosure and the water bowl.
rules.title: Litter next to water

rules.explanation: An all-mesh roof gives no shade; cats can overheat in summer sun.
rules.remediation: Add a partial or full solid cover, shade cloth, or place the catio in afternoon shade. Keep water available.
rules.title: No shade in a hot climate

rules.explanation: Cats use a catio more when part of it stays dry and shaded.
rules.remediation: Cover part of the roof (a partial polycarbonate cover is cheap and bright).
rules.title: No rain or sun cover

rules.explanation: Snow collects on mesh and solid roofs alike; heavy snow can sag or break light framing.
rules.remediation: Plan to clear snow, add rafters, or have the roof framing reviewed for your snow load.
rules.title: Snow load on the roof

rules.explanation: Light enclosures and solid roof panels catch wind.
rules.remediation: Anchor the frame to the ground or deck at every corner and fasten roof panels at every purlin; consider professional review.
rules.title: High-wind site
